segment_reference_payload.description: Segment sends Identify and Track events to Qualtrics via the Actions-based destination (slug: actions-qualtrics). Identify events create or update contacts in the Qualtrics XM Directory using the XM Directory API v3. Track events record contact transactions (behavioral events) against the contact record in XM Directory. The destination uses the Qualtrics REST API v3 with X-API-TOKEN header authentication and requires a Datacenter ID for endpoint routing. Segment's Actions-based Qualtrics integration supports configurable field mappings via the 'Create and/or update contact in XM Directory' action, allowing users to define which Segment event fields map to Qualtrics contact fields, embedded data, and transaction properties.

datacenterId.description: Qualtrics datacenter ID (e.g., 'iad1', 'sjc1', 'fra1') used to construct the API base URL. Found in Qualtrics Account Settings under Qualtrics IDs.

directoryId.description: XM Directory ID (format: POOL_xxxxxxxxxxxxx) identifying the target contact directory for contact creation and transaction recording.

auth.description: Qualtrics API Token from Account Settings > Qualtrics IDs. The token authenticates all API interactions and scopes operations to the authenticated user's brand. Segment requires a token generated by a Business Tier customer with Public API access.

batch_support.description: Segment sends each event individually to Qualtrics XM Directory API. Contact creation/update and transaction recording are separate API calls.

contact_lookup.description: Qualtrics first attempts to find an existing contact using extRef (externalDataReference), email, or phone. If no match is found, a new contact is created. If a match is found, the existing contact is updated.

mailing_list_association.description: If a mailingListId is configured in Segment destination settings, the contact is also added to the specified mailing list after creation/update.

identify.mapping_notes: Segment maps Identify traits to Qualtrics contact fields. Standard contact fields (firstName, lastName, email, phone, language, extRef) are mapped directly. The userId from the Identify call maps to the extRef (externalDataReference) field, which serves as the primary external identifier for contact deduplication and lookup. All remaining traits that do not match standard contact fields are stored as embeddedData key-value pairs. Numeric and boolean trait values are coerced to strings for embeddedData storage. If a mailingListId is configured, the contact is associated with the specified mailing list.

contact_resolution.description: Before recording a transaction, Qualtrics resolves the contact using extRef (userId), email, or phone. If no contact is found and sufficient identification fields are provided, a new contact is created automatically.

track.mapping_notes: Segment Track events are recorded as contact transactions in Qualtrics XM Directory. The event name ('Survey Completed') is not directly stored as a transaction field — instead, the transaction 'data' object contains all event properties as key-value pairs. The transactionDate is mapped from the event timestamp. The contact is resolved using the userId (mapped to extRef) before the transaction is recorded against the contact record. All property values are coerced to strings in the transaction data. If the contact does not exist and lookup fields (extRef, email, phone) are provided, Qualtrics can auto-create the contact before recording the transaction.

track_survey_response_event.description: When Qualtrics is configured as a Segment Source (via the Qualtrics Segment Task), survey response data flows from Qualtrics into Segment as Track events. This represents the reverse data flow — Qualtrics sending survey completion data to Segment for downstream routing. The Qualtrics Source uses server-side track and identify methods.

properties.Q3_feedback: The new dashboard redesign is excellent.

track_survey_response_event.mapping_notes: This event is generated by Qualtrics as a Source, not consumed by Qualtrics as a Destination. The Qualtrics Segment Task maps survey response data to Segment track events. Survey questions and responses become event properties with configurable field names. The userId can be sourced from the survey response's embedded data, external data reference, or a custom piped text value configured in the Qualtrics Segment Task setup. The context.library.name is 'qualtrics' since the event originates from the Qualtrics platform.

rudderstack_expected_payload.description: RudderStack sends Identify and Track events to Qualtrics via the Transformer service (port 9090), which handles field mapping and payload formatting. Identify events create or update contacts in the Qualtrics XM Directory using the same XM Directory API v3 endpoints. Track events record contact transactions against the resolved contact record. RudderStack adds envelope fields (rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt) to internal event representation but the Transformer strips these before sending to Qualtrics' API. The destination is classified as a cloud destination processed through the Router's HTTP transport.

datacenterId.description: Qualtrics datacenter ID configured in RudderStack dashboard destination settings. Stored in backend-config and delivered to the Transformer during event processing.

directoryId.description: XM Directory ID for the target contact directory. Configured in RudderStack dashboard destination settings.

auth.description: Qualtrics API Token configured in RudderStack dashboard destination settings. Stored in backend-config and delivered to the Transformer during event processing.

batch_support.description: RudderStack sends each event individually to Qualtrics XM Directory API. The Router processes events one at a time for this destination type.

RudderStack envelope fields (rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt) are present in the internal pipeline representation but are stripped by the Transformer before delivery to Qualtrics' API.

The only differences from Segment-sourced events are: (1) RudderStack-specific envelope fields (rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt) present in the internal pipeline, (2) context.library.name is 'rudder-sdk-js' instead of 'qualtrics' when sourced from RudderStack SDK. rudderstack_envelope_fields.description: RudderStack-specific fields present in internal pipeline representation but stripped by Transformer before Qualtrics API delivery.

fields.rudderId: UUID assigned by RudderStack Gateway during event ingestion — unique per event instance in the RudderStack pipeline
fields.originalTimestamp: Client-side timestamp from the SDK, preserved separately from server-assigned timestamp
fields.sentAt: Timestamp when the SDK dispatched the event to the Gateway
fields.receivedAt: Timestamp when the Gateway received the event

contact_directory_mapping.description: Qualtrics XM Directory is the central contact database for the Qualtrics Experience Management platform. The Identify call maps user traits to Qualtrics contact fields and embeddedData. The XM Directory API v3 provides create, read, update, and delete operations on contacts, with deduplication based on configurable identity fields (extRef, email, phone). Contacts stored in XM Directory can be targeted for survey distributions, referenced in survey flow logic via embedded data, and segmented for analysis.

external_data_reference.description: External Data Reference — the primary external identifier for a contact in XM Directory. Mapped from the event's userId field. This field is the recommended deduplication key for contacts created via API, as it uniquely identifies a contact across systems. If userId is not available, anonymousId may be used as a fallback depending on destination configuration.

contact_id.description: Qualtrics-assigned contact ID. Generated by Qualtrics upon contact creation. Used for subsequent update and transaction API calls. Not provided in the inbound Segment/RudderStack event — resolved by Qualtrics during contact lookup.

deduplication_strategy.description: Qualtrics XM Directory supports configurable deduplication rules managed by directory administrators. The integration first attempts to find an existing contact by extRef, then by email, then by phone. If multiple matches are found, the most recently updated contact is used. Deduplication settings can be customized at the directory level to use different field combinations.
lookup_order: email — secondary lookup if extRef not found or not provided
phone — tertiary lookup if neither extRef nor email match
deduplication_strategy.on_no_match: Create new contact with provided fields
deduplication_strategy.on_single_match: Update existing contact with new field values

standard_contact_fields.description: Qualtrics XM Directory defines a set of standard contact fields that receive special treatment in the platform. These fields are displayed prominently in contact profiles, available as built-in distribution variables, and support structured validation. Segment/RudderStack traits matching these field names are mapped directly to the standard fields.

firstName.description: Contact's first name. Used in survey personalization (e.g., 'Hi ${e://Field/firstName}'). Displayed in contact profiles and distribution recipient lists.

lastName.description: Contact's last name. Combined with firstName for full name display in Qualtrics UI.

email.description: Contact's email address. Used for email survey distributions and as a secondary deduplication key. Must be a valid email format.

phone.description: Contact's phone number. Used for SMS survey distributions. Accepted formats vary by region (E.164 recommended).

language.description: Contact's preferred language code (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'ja'). Used to select the localized version of a survey when multi-language surveys are configured.

unsubscribed.description: Whether the contact has opted out of survey distributions. When true, the contact will not receive email or SMS survey invitations from this directory.

embedded_data_mapping.description: Any trait not matching a standard contact field is stored as embedded data on the contact record. Embedded data provides flexible key-value storage for custom attributes that can be referenced in survey flow logic, used for contact segmentation, and piped into survey questions. Qualtrics embedded data keys are case-insensitive for lookup purposes but preserve the original casing when stored.

mapping_rules.trait_to_embedded_data: All traits not matching standard fields (firstName, lastName, email, phone, language, extRef, unsubscribed) are stored as embedded data
mapping_rules.key_format: Preserved as-is from trait key name (no case conversion applied by default)

value_coercion.boolean: Converted to string representation (e.g., true → 'true', false → 'false')
value_coercion.null: Stored as empty string or omitted depending on directory settings

mapping_rules.max_key_length: No documented hard limit; recommended to keep under 200 characters
mapping_rules.max_value_length: No documented hard limit; recommended to keep under 10000 characters
mapping_rules.reserved_fields: Do not use 'Points' as an embedded data key — it is a reserved field in XM Directory

embedded_data_mapping.parity_status: Equivalent — both Segment and RudderStack store non-standard traits as embedded data with the same value coercion rules. Key names are preserved without case conversion.

mailing_list_association.description: Contacts can be associated with one or more mailing lists within the XM Directory. Mailing lists are used to organize contacts for survey distributions. When a mailingListId is configured in the destination settings, the integration adds the contact to the specified list after creation or update.
mailing_list_association.segment_behavior: If mailingListId is configured in Segment destination settings, contact is added to the mailing list after create/update
mailing_list_association.rudderstack_behavior: If mailingListId is configured in RudderStack destination settings, contact is added to the mailing list after create/update
mailing_list_association.parity_status: Equivalent — both platforms support mailing list association via destination-level configuration

contact_directory_mapping.parity_status: Equivalent — both Segment and RudderStack map Identify traits to Qualtrics XM Directory contact fields using the same mapping rules. Standard contact fields are mapped directly, userId maps to extRef for deduplication, and remaining traits are stored as embedded data with string coercion. The final contact payload sent to Qualtrics' API is identical between platforms after the Transformer strips RudderStack envelope fields.

survey_response_association.description: Qualtrics uses contact transactions to associate behavioral events and survey responses with contact profiles in XM Directory. Track events are recorded as transactions against the resolved contact, creating a timeline of interactions that can be used for survey targeting, contact segmentation, and analytics. The transaction data is accessible in the contact's timeline view in the Qualtrics XM Directory UI.

transaction_data_model.description: Each contact transaction consists of a transactionDate and a data object containing key-value pairs. The data object stores all event properties from the Track call.

transactionDate.description: Date and time of the transaction. Mapped from the event timestamp in ISO-8601 format.

data.description: Transaction data containing all event properties. All values are coerced to strings. The event name itself is not stored as a separate transaction field — it should be included as a property (e.g., 'event_name': 'Survey Completed') if needed for downstream filtering.

contact_resolution_for_transactions.description: Before recording a transaction, the integration must resolve the target contact. Resolution uses the same lookup strategy as Identify: extRef (userId), then email, then phone. If the Segment/RudderStack Track event includes a contactId (from a previous Identify response stored in the pipeline), it can be used directly to skip the lookup step.

lookup_fields.secondary: email (from properties.email or previously resolved contact)
lookup_fields.tertiary: phone (from properties.phone or previously resolved contact)

auto_create_contact.description: If no existing contact is found and sufficient identification fields are provided (at minimum: extRef or email), the Qualtrics API can automatically create a new contact before recording the transaction. This behavior depends on the destination configuration.
auto_create_contact.segment_behavior: Auto-create contact if contactId is not supplied but extRef/email/phone are available
auto_create_contact.rudderstack_behavior: Same auto-create behavior via Transformer mapping

contact_resolution_for_transactions.parity_status: Equivalent — both platforms resolve contacts using the same field priority and support auto-creation

survey_targeting_with_transactions.description: Contact transactions enable event-based survey targeting in Qualtrics. When configuring survey distribution triggers or Website/App Feedback intercepts, administrators can reference transaction history to target contacts who have performed specific actions. For example, a satisfaction survey can be triggered for contacts whose transaction data includes 'product_area: Dashboard' and 'satisfaction_score < 3'.
targeting_examples: Show survey when contact has a transaction with product_area = 'Dashboard'
Trigger NPS survey when contact has completed 10+ transactions in the last 30 days
Send follow-up survey when latest transaction has satisfaction_score < 3
Target contacts whose transaction data includes 'channel: email' for distribution preference research

embedded_data_vs_transactions.description: Embedded data (from Identify) represents static/current contact attributes, while transactions (from Track) represent temporal behavioral events. Both are used in Qualtrics for survey targeting and analysis, but they serve different purposes: embedded data for profile-based segmentation, transactions for behavior-based triggering.
embedded_data_vs_transactions.identify_embedded_data: Current state of the contact (e.g., plan: enterprise, npsScore: 8)
embedded_data_vs_transactions.track_transactions: Historical events/actions (e.g., Survey Completed on 2026-03-15 with score 4)

survey_targeting_with_transactions.parity_status: Equivalent — both platforms create the same transaction data structure, enabling identical survey targeting capabilities in Qualtrics

nps_csat_response_integration.description: Qualtrics is widely used for NPS (Net Promoter Score) and CSAT (Customer Satisfaction) surveys. Survey response data can flow bi-directionally: (1) As Track events to Qualtrics to record the interaction context, and (2) From Qualtrics back to Segment/RudderStack as survey response events for downstream analytics and action.

nps_survey_flow.inbound_track: Track event 'Survey Completed' with nps_score property → recorded as transaction in XM Directory
nps_survey_flow.outbound_response: Qualtrics Source sends 'Survey Response Recorded' track event with question-level response data

csat_survey_flow.inbound_track: Track event with satisfaction_score property → recorded as transaction
csat_survey_flow.outbound_response: Qualtrics Source sends satisfaction data as track event properties

nps_csat_response_integration.parity_status: Equivalent — NPS and CSAT data flows use the same event format in both Segment and RudderStack integrations

survey_response_association.parity_status: Equivalent — both Segment and RudderStack record Track events as contact transactions in Qualtrics XM Directory using the same API endpoint and data format. Transaction properties are coerced to strings identically. Contact resolution before transaction recording follows the same lookup priority.

context_library_difference.description: The SDK library name in context differs between Segment and RudderStack. This field is NOT sent to Qualtrics' API but is present in the internal event representation.
context_library_difference.segment: context.library.name = 'analytics.js' (or analytics-ios, analytics-android, qualtrics for Source events)
context_library_difference.impact: No impact on Qualtrics payloads — context.library is not forwarded to Qualtrics' XM Directory API. Difference is only visible in the source pipeline.

message_id_difference.description: Event message ID format differs between Segment and RudderStack. This field is NOT sent to Qualtrics' API.
message_id_difference.segment: messageId generated by analytics.js SDK (UUID v4 format)
message_id_difference.rudderstack: messageId generated by rudder-sdk SDK (UUID v4 format, different generation strategy)
message_id_difference.impact: No impact on Qualtrics payloads — messageId is used internally for deduplication in the pipeline, not forwarded to Qualtrics.

rudderstack_additional_fields.description: RudderStack includes additional envelope fields in the internal event representation that are not present in Segment events. These fields are stripped by the Transformer before delivery to Qualtrics.

fields.rudderId: Unique event instance ID assigned by RudderStack Gateway

rudderstack_additional_fields.impact: No impact on Qualtrics payloads — all additional fields are stripped during transformation. The final payload sent to Qualtrics is identical between Segment and RudderStack.

destination_settings.description: Configuration fields required to set up Qualtrics as a destination in both Segment and RudderStack.

apiToken.description: Qualtrics API Token from Account Settings > Qualtrics IDs. Required for all API interactions. Business Tier required for Segment integration.

datacenterId.description: Qualtrics datacenter ID (e.g., 'iad1', 'sjc1', 'fra1'). Determines the API base URL for all requests.

directoryId.description: XM Directory ID (format: POOL_xxxxxxxxxxxxx). Identifies the target contact directory.

mailingListId.description: Optional mailing list ID (format: CG_xxxxxxxxxxxxx). If provided, contacts are added to this mailing list after creation/update.

apiToken.description: Qualtrics API Token — same key format as Segment configuration. Configured in RudderStack dashboard destination settings.

datacenterId.description: Qualtrics datacenter ID — determines API routing. Same datacenter ID as Segment configuration.

directoryId.description: XM Directory ID for the target contact directory.

mailingListId.description: Optional mailing list ID for contact association.

destination_settings.parity_status: Equivalent — both platforms require the same core configuration fields (apiToken, datacenterId, directoryId) with optional mailingListId. Segment's Actions-based destination provides additional configurable field mapping capabilities through its UI that RudderStack handles via the Transformer's built-in mapping logic.

notes: Qualtrics is an Experience Management (XM) platform in the Surveys category, providing survey creation, distribution, and analytics capabilities. This payload parity fixture covers Track and Identify event types — the two call types supported by the Qualtrics Segment/RudderStack integration. Key parity observations: (1) Endpoint and payload format — both Segment and RudderStack send events to the same Qualtrics XM Directory API v3 endpoints using JSON format with X-API-TOKEN header authentication and datacenter-based URL routing; (2) Contact directory mapping — Identify traits are mapped to Qualtrics contact fields with standard fields (firstName, lastName, email, phone, language) mapped directly and remaining traits stored as embeddedData key-value pairs; userId maps to extRef (externalDataReference) as the primary external identifier for contact deduplication; (3) Survey response association — Track events are recorded as contact transactions in XM Directory, creating a behavioral timeline linked to the contact profile; transaction data contains event properties as string-coerced key-value pairs with the event timestamp as transactionDate; (4) Mailing list association — both platforms support optional mailing list association via destination-level configuration (mailingListId); (5) Bi-directional integration — Qualtrics supports both inbound data (Identify/Track to XM Directory) and outbound data (survey responses as Track events via Qualtrics Source/Task); (6) NPS/CSAT integration — survey score data flows through the pipeline in both directions, enabling closed-loop feedback workflows; (7) Context library difference — context.library.name differs ('analytics.js' vs 'rudder-sdk-js') but this field is not forwarded to Qualtrics; (8) Envelope fields — RudderStack's additional envelope fields (rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt) are present in the internal pipeline but stripped by the Transformer before delivery; (9) Final payload parity — after transformation, the payloads delivered to Qualtrics' XM Directory API are identical between Segment and RudderStack; (10) Segment has an Actions-based variant of the Qualtrics destination (slug: 'actions-qualtrics') with configurable field mappings, while RudderStack handles equivalent mapping through the Transformer service. RudderStack source: Transformer service cloud destination handler for QUALTRICS.
